title: Riyadh Capital Review 2026: Is It Regulated or a Red Flag?
description: Riyadh Capital review: its claims about AI trading, a $250 minimum and a 4.6/5 rating, and what we could and could not confirm.
author: James Whitmore
excerpt: Riyadh Capital promotes AI trading with a $250 minimum and a 4.6/5 rating, but names no operator or regulator.
content:
Riyadh Capital is presented as an AI trading platform with automated trades, a demo account and a $250 starting point. Its page names no operator, no regulator and no licence number, and the only performance figure is a 4.6/5 rating with no named source.

The name suggests a capital firm, but the page names no company and no regulator. The asset table lists bonds only. This review sets out what the page says and what we could not confirm.

Riyadh Capital at a Glance

Here is what the platform's own page states and what it leaves out.

Platform typeAI-assisted trading with automatic and manual modes
Minimum deposit$250, currency not named
FeesNo fees stated. No schedule given
Payment methodsPayPal, Skrill, cards and bank transfer, with other options unnamed
WithdrawalsUsually within 24 hours. No limits given
SupportDescribed as 24/7, with no channels listed
Regulator or licenceNot stated
OperatorNot named

Items marked as stated come from the platform's own page. We have not tested the platform.

Is Riyadh Capital Legit? What the Claims Show

Automation and signals

The page says AI and machine learning generate signals and can place trades automatically, with a manual mode for users who prefer control. It does not describe the strategy, the model or the risk limits, so the claim cannot be tested from the page.

Performance and ratings

The page refers to strong results and a high success rate, but gives no return figures, time period, sample size or method. The 4.6/5 rating has no named source or review count.

Asset coverage

The asset claims are not consistent across the page. The name suggests a capital firm, but the page names no company and no regulator. The asset table lists bonds only. A user cannot tell which markets are actually offered before signing up.

Costs Worth Knowing

The page states a $250 minimum deposit and says there are no registration, transaction or withdrawal fees, but it gives no fee schedule, spreads or payment-provider charges.

Our standard minimum deposit for this review is 250 in the reader's local currency: AUD 250 in Australia, GBP 250 in the UK and EUR 250 in the EU. The page states $250 and does not name a currency, so confirm the exact amount in the terms before you deposit.

Who Is Behind the Brand

The page names no legal entity, company number or address. Its sign-up buttons all link to coinpulse.cc, a third-party domain, and the page does not disclose whether that link earns the publisher a commission.

Before You Register: A Short Checklist

  • Find the legal company behind Riyadh Capital and check it against your national regulator's register.
  • Ask for a written fee schedule, including spreads and withdrawal charges.
  • Ask for dated, verifiable performance records rather than a single rating.
  • Start with the smallest amount you can afford to lose, and use any demo account first.

Risks to Keep in Mind

The main risk is an unnamed operator, because a user has no clear party to hold to account. The mismatch in the asset and payment claims adds to that risk. Automation changes how trades are placed, not whether they can lose money.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is the minimum deposit for Riyadh Capital?

The page states $250 but does not name the currency. Confirm the amount and currency in the terms before you pay.

Is Riyadh Capital regulated?

The page names no regulator or licence number. Search the regulator's register for the company that runs the service.

Does Riyadh Capital charge fees?

The page says there are no fees but gives no schedule for spreads, withdrawals or other costs. Read the full terms first.

Does automation remove the risk of losing money?

No. Automation changes how trades are placed, not whether they can lose money.

Our Verdict on Riyadh Capital

Riyadh Capital's page makes broad claims without naming an operator, a regulator or verifiable results. Our rating reflects these gaps. We will revisit it once those details can be confirmed. Start only with money you can afford to lose.
